title: The Resume window, before and after

steps.path: The sessions arrow at the top of the window, then Resume
steps.headline: Clicking a conversation now shows it, instead of opening controls inside its card.
steps.changed: The window is twice as wide. The card you clicked lifts to the top of the right half and floats there while you read what was actually said; the model, the two switches and Resume sit in a card at the foot, where a real conversation puts its message box. The cards in the list never open up any more, so the list stops jumping.
steps.notice: The conversations here are the workbench's invented ones. The layout, spacing and controls are the real ones, and this is the real app running the real transcript reader.
steps.risk: Below 640 px — a phone, a narrow window — and in the Android app, it stays exactly as it is on the left. Android has no transcript reader, so the panel would only ever show an error there.

steps.path: The same window, with the stress fixture's long titles and heavy tagging
steps.headline: The same window against long names, many tags, and a list too long to fit.
steps.changed: Nothing new here — this is the check that the two halves hold when the list is full and the titles run past their width.
steps.notice: The first row in this fixture cannot be resumed and cannot be read either: its transcript has not synced to this device yet, so clicking it does nothing and the panel stays on the row below.
steps.risk: A conversation whose project FOLDER is missing behaves differently: it now opens and reads normally, and the foot card explains why there is no Resume button rather than offering one that cannot work.
